items.abstract: <jats:p>Low-light image enhancement is one of the fundamental tasks in image processing. While various methods have been proposed, they often fail to produce visually appealing results. In this paper, we aim to make use of the both semantic information and HSV color space in the whole process, to generate results with clear details, good contrast and no color distortion. To preserve the semantic information during the enhancement, we introduce an unsupervised semantic segmentation network requiring no expensive segmentation annotation. Furthermore, we design a HSV loss to preserve the hue and saturation of the original image, aiming at well improving the color distortion. The HSV loss merges with other non-reference loss functions as the total loss during the training. Our method performs well for a wide variety of images, and achieves better quality both in objective and subjective assessment, compared with the state-of-the-art methods.</jats:p>

items.abstract: Low-light image enhancement aims to recover visually pleasing and structurally faithful images from underexposed inputs. Existing methods in the HVI color space still lack effective multi-scale modeling and spatial-frequency integration. Here we present FPA-Net, a dual-branch network that integrates complex-valued frequency-domain modeling, multi-scale dual attention, and position-aware cross attention for robust low-light enhancement. The method jointly optimizes illumination and chromaticity branches to suppress artifacts and preserve color consistency. Extensive experiments on LOL-v1, LOL-v2, and MIT-5K datasets show that FPA-Net achieves state-of-the-art performance with 24.72 dB PSNR and 0.863 SSIM on LOL-v1. This work provides a valid solution for frequency-aware and position-guided low-light enhancement in the HVI space and supports reliable visual perception for real-world applications.The code is available at https://github.com/ll1zh/FPA-Net
title: FPA-Net:Frequency and Position-Aware Deep Network for Low-Light Image Enhancement in HVI Color Space
